(i) the robot can learn to adapt its dialogue strategy to a user’s emotional state and (ii) this can lead to a more enjoyable experience for the user.

the inclusion of emotion recognition in the dialogue management module of a Reinforcement Learning based dialogue manager for the purpose of improving user engagement in a cognitive training task, such as the 2048 game, is a promising avenue for future research.
we can: (i) use the facial expressions of a user to recognize emotions, and (ii) use the recognized emotions to modulate robot dialogue in order to improve the user's enjoyment of the 2048 game.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to use recognized emotions to improve a cognitive game scenario, and how to use a dialogue management system based on RL to improve the interaction with a robot.
how to use recognized emotional states of the user to improve the user’s experience in a cognitive training game scenario.
the development of a robot companion that is capable of recognizing human emotions and adapting its behaviour in order to make cognitive training games more engaging for the users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the robot’s dialogue management module is able to recognize the emotions expressed by the user during a cognitive task, and is able to adapt its dialogue responses to the user’s emotions.
our approach is capable of adapting the dialogue strategy in order to increase the user’s enjoyment and thus, the effectiveness of the training session.
our proposed method is capable of adapting its dialogue responses to the emotional state of the user, and that this adaptation is beneficial to the user.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed a system that is able to recognize the emotions of a human user and adapt its dialogue in order to make the game more enjoyable for the user.
we propose a method for using emotions to improve user experience in a cognitive task.
we are attempting to build an Affective Companion Robot (ACR) that can recognize the emotions of its user in a cognitive game scenario and adapt its dialogue responses accordingly.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the robot’s ability to recognize emotions in the user, and adapt its behaviour to make the task more enjoyable, is perceived as a highly desirable trait by users, even if the task itself is not inherently enjoyable.
it can be beneficial to incorporate recognized emotions in a dialogue system, and that this can be done without the need for extensive training data.

by integrating emotion recognition with RL, we can create a robot that is capable of adapting to its users in a way that is beneficial to them, in this case by making the cognitive training task more enjoyable for the user.
